# Make locus plots for two highlighted examples

### Gene expression for linked genes
```{r fig.height = 10, eval = F}
# obtain gene expression matrix in CPMs across lung immune cells
rna_counts <- readRDS("~/projects/Lung_scMultiomics_paper/data/pseudobulk_rna_CPM.RDS")
rna_metadata <- readRDS("~/projects/Lung_scMultiomics_paper/output/u19_multiomics/output/u19_rna/u19_rna_cell_metadata.RDS")
ct_rna <- c("Naive_B", "Memory_B", "NK", "CD8_T", "CD4_T", "Th17", "Treg")
rna_counts <- t(rna_counts[rna_metadata$tissue.ident == "lungs", ])
rna_metadata <- rna_metadata[rna_metadata$tissue.ident == "lungs", ]
rna_ranges <- promoters(proj@geneAnnotation$genes)
rna_gr <- GRanges(seqnames = seqnames(rna_ranges),
                  IRanges(start = start(rna_ranges)-25000,
                          end = start(rna_ranges)))
mcols(rna_gr) <- mcols(rna_ranges)
# group count matrix by pseudo-bulk
rna_countByCT <-
  lapply(unique(rna_metadata$CellType), function(i) {
    rowSums(rna_counts[, rna_metadata$CellType == i])
    })
rna_countByCT <- t(do.call(rbind, rna_countByCT))
colnames(rna_countByCT) <- unique(rna_metadata$CellType)
metadata <- left_join(
  data.frame(CellType = colnames(rna_countByCT)),
  rna_metadata %>% mutate(Sample = core_ID) %>%
    dplyr::select(CellType, batch, major, Sample, tissue.ident) %>% 
    distinct(),
  by = "CellType")

d_rna <- DGEList(counts = rna_countByCT, 
             remove.zeros = TRUE)
rna_counts <- cpm(d_rna, normalized.lib.sizes = TRUE, log = TRUE)#FALSE)
rna_counts <- rna_counts[, colnames(rna_counts) != "Other"]
```
```{r}
rna_counts <- readRDS("~/projects/Lung_scMultiomics_paper/data/lung_RNA_CPM_by_CellType.RDS")

plotTracks(list(dt2, gat),
```

### Plotting RNA counts across cell types for two genes (LRRC32 & CCR4 & GLB1)

```{r}
f_rna <-readRDS("../../output/output_dir/remove_dup/pseudobulk_RNA_counts_E2G.RDS")
# 2. Convert raw pseudobulk counts to CPM
  rna_counts <- apply(f_rna, 2, function(x) {
    (x / sum(x)) * 1e6
  })

# Verify CPM sums to 1 million per sample (column)
colSums(rna_counts)

toplot = c("LRRC32", "CCR4", "GLB1") # "TNFRSF11A", "ARRDC1", "CEBPA", "DPH7", "SLC7A10")
metadata <-data.frame(
  sample = colnames(rna_counts),
  CellType = unlist(
    lapply(colnames(rna_counts), function(i) {
      words = strsplit(i, "_")[[1]][-1]
      return(paste(words, collapse = "_"))
      })))
for(i in 1:length(toplot)){
  metadata[, toplot[i]] <- data.frame(rna_counts[rownames(rna_counts) %in% toplot[i], ])
}

metadata$CellType[metadata$CellType == "Th17/CD4_T"] <- "memCD4_T"

ggplot(metadata %>% 
         pivot_longer(-2:-1, names_to = "Gene",
                      values_to = "Counts") %>%
         filter(CellType != "Other") %>%
         mutate(CellType = factor(CellType, levels = gsub("[.]", "/", ct_order))),
       aes(y = Counts,
           x = CellType,
           fill = CellType)) + 
  geom_boxplot() + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_atac[-1]) + 
  ylab("RNA counts") + 
  facet_grid(Gene ~ .) + 
  theme_pub(base_size = 13) + xlab("") + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 0.6))
```


## Locuszoom plots for specific examples

```{r}
# prepare RNA expression counts
multiome_p2g <- readRDS("")
```



```{r}
library(GenomicFeatures) #  Making and manipulating annotations
library(Gviz) # R package used to visualize track plots
library(GenomicInteractions) # visualize HiC loops
library(AnnotationDbi) # match gene ID to gene symbol
library(org.Hs.eg.db) # match gene ID to gene symbol
library(mapgen)

f <- readRDS("~/cluster/projects/u19_multiomics/data/coa_gp3_finemapping_gwas_L5.rds")
f_gr <- GRanges(seqnames = paste0("chr", f$chr),
                IRanges(start = f$pos,
                        end = f$pos+1))
mcols(f_gr) <- f[, -4:-1]
#liftOver to hg38
ch=import.chain("~/resources/genomes/chain_files/hg19ToHg38.over.chain")
seqlevelsStyle(f_gr) <- "UCSC"
f_hg38_gr<- unlist(liftOver(f_gr, ch))
f_input <- data.frame(f_hg38_gr) %>%
  mutate(chr = as.integer(gsub("chr", "", seqnames)),
         pos = start) %>%
  dplyr::select(snp, chr, pos, pval, zscore, susie_pip, locus, CS)
  

finemapstats <- process_finemapping_sumstats(f_input, 
                                             snp = 'snp', 
                                             chr = 'chr', 
                                             pos = 'pos', 
                                             pip = 'susie_pip', 
                                             pval = 'pval', 
                                             zscore = 'zscore', 
                                             cs = 'CS', 
                                             locus = 'locus',  
                                             pip.thresh = 0)
# force PIPs for SNPs not in a credible set to be zero
finemapstats$pip[finemapstats$cs == 0] <- 0
# load gene/transcript tracks
gtf_file <- '/project2/xinhe/shared_data/gencode/GRCh38/gencode.v21.annotation.gtf.gz'
genomic.annots <- make_genomic_annots(gtf_file)
gene.annots <- genomic.annots$genes
txdb <- loadDb("~/cluster/projects/u19_multiomics/mapgen/gencode.v21.hg38.annotation.gtf.sqlite")
# load LD reference panel
bigSNP <- bigsnpr::snp_attach(rdsfile = '/project2/xinhe/1kg/bigsnpr/hg38/EUR_1kg.rds')

# load peak bigwig files
fpath = "~/cluster/projects/u19_multiomics/analyses/u19_peaks_tissue/GroupBigWigs/CellGroup"
peak_counts <- list()
for(i in list.files(fpath)[grepl("Lung", list.files(fpath))]){
  idx = strsplit(i, "-")[[1]][1]
  idx = gsub("Lung_", "", idx)
  peak_counts[[idx]] <- rtracklayer::import(file.path(fpath, i))
}
names(peak_counts) <- gsub("/", ".", names(peak_counts))

```


```{r, fig.height = 10, fig.width = 9}
p2g_list <- split(multiome_p2g, multiome_p2g$CellType)
loops_list <- list()
for(c in names(p2g_list)){
  loop_gr <- GRanges(p2g_list[[c]]$ref_gr)
  names(loop_gr) <- NULL
  mcols(loop_gr) <- 
     data.frame(p2g_list[[c]]) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(score = E2G.Score.qnorm * 10,
             promoter_start = TargetGeneTSS,
             promoter_end = promoter_start,
             gene_name = TargetGene) %>%
    dplyr::select(promoter_start, promoter_end, gene_name, score)
  loops_list[[c]] <- loop_gr
}

loops_full <- lapply(loops_list, process_loop_data)

# LRRC32
loops_idx <- lapply(loops_full[gsub("/", ".", ct_order[c(1,8,6)])], function(i){
  match(c(76588363), start(i)) 
})
# make some shifts
#loops_idx$Naive_B[2] = loops_idx$Naive_B[2] - 2
loops_idx[[2]] = loops_idx[[2]] + 2
loops_idx[[3]] = loops_idx[[3]] + 1
loops_col <- lapply(gsub("/", ".", ct_order[c(1,8,6)]), function(i){
  col = rep("grey", length(loops_full[[i]]))
  col[as.numeric(loops_idx[[i]])] <- "red"
  return(col)
  })
names(loops_col) <- gsub("/", ".", ct_order[c(1,8,6)])

# CCR4
loops_idx <- lapply(loops_full[gsub("/", ".", ct_order[6:8])], function(i){
  match(c(32963768, 33005974), start(i))
})
#loops_idx$CD8.CD4_T[2] <- NA
loops_col <- lapply(gsub("/", ".", ct_order[6:8]), function(i){
  col = rep("grey", length(loops_full[[i]]))
  col[as.numeric(loops_idx[[i]])] <- "red"
  return(col)
  })
names(loops_col) <- gsub("/", ".", ct_order[6:8])

# TNFSF4
loops_idx <- lapply(loops_full[gsub("/", ".", ct_order[c(1,2)])], function(i){
  match(173202304, start(i))
})

loops_col <- lapply(gsub("/", ".", ct_order[c(1,2)]), function(i){
  col = rep("grey", length(loops_full[[i]]))
  col[as.numeric(loops_idx[[i]])] <- "red"
  return(col)
  })
names(loops_col) <- gsub("/", ".", ct_order[c(1,2)])

peak_x10 <- lapply(peak_counts, function(i){
  mcols(i)$score <- mcols(i)$score * 10

names(peak_x10)[8] <- "memCD4_T"

selected_genes <- c("CCR4")# "TCF7", "CCL20", "LRRC32", "CCR4")

pdf("data/plots/CCR4_locusplot2.pdf", width = 130/25.4, height = 160/25.4)
#par(mfrow = c(2, 1))
for(i in loci_idx[1]){
  #ct = gsub("/", ".", topCellType)[i]

             #region = as.character(gr_peaks_sub[loci_idx] + 20000),
               #"chr9:137556174-137656674",
             # region = "chr11:76580000-76678500",
             "chr3:32940000-33020000",
             #"chr1:173200000-173302804",
             #"chr5:134050000-134160000",
```

```{r, eval = F}
# Literature search:
# 
# The ligand-receptor pair CCL20-CCR6 is responsible for the chemotaxis of dendritic cells (DC), effector/memory T-cells and B-cells and plays an important role at skin and mucosal surfaces under homeostatic and inflammatory conditions, as well as in pathology, including cancer and various autoimmune diseases (PubMed:21376174).
# `
# CXCR5 is a protein receptor, a C-X-C chemokine receptor type 5, that plays a crucial role in immune cell trafficking and development, particularly in B and T cell lymphocytes. It is involved in B cell homing, T follicular helper (Tfh) cell development, and the formation of germinal centers in secondary lymphoid organs. CXCR5 is a key receptor for the chemokine CXCL13. 
# 
# EMSY is a human protein encoded by the EMSY gene. It's a chromatin remodeler that promotes a BRCAness phenotype by regulating homologous recombination repair (HRR). EMSY also suppresses the type I interferon response and innate immunity. 
# 
# TLR10 is a functional receptor expressed by B cells and plasmacytoid dendritic cells. It plays a role in regulating immune responses, particularly in suppressing pro-inflammatory signaling pathways. It potentially suppresses the activation of NF-κB and MAPK pathways. 
# 
# TBX21, also known as T-bet, is a gene that encodes a T-box transcription factor involved in the immune system, particularly in the development and function of Th1 cells. It plays a role in both innate and adaptive immunity, including T-cell homing to pro-inflammatory sites. TBX21 is also implicated in various diseases, including asthma and Alzheimer's disease. 
# 
# CCR4 is a protein, specifically a C-C chemokine receptor, that plays a role in the immune system. It's expressed on various T cell subsets, including Th2, Treg, and Th17 cells. CCR4 is also involved in recruiting these T cells to different tissues, including the skin and tumor microenvironments.
# 
# PRKCQ encodes protein kinase C theta (PKC-θ), a protein involved in T-cell signaling and immune responses. It is a member of the serine/threonine kinases family and is primarily expressed in hematopoietic cells, particularly T lymphocytes and platelets. PKC-θ plays a crucial role in T-cell activation, proliferation, and differentiation, and its activity is essential for downstream signaling pathways.
```
